### What does this PR do?

This is a follow-up to #8482 (the `mori` checkpoint engine) and builds on it; only the last commit is new. It adds `export: shard`. Each trainer rank sends only its own shards from the training engine's `get_per_tensor_param_shard()`, in bf16 and using the contract in `verl/workers/engine/spec.py`, so the trainer no longer all-gathers every parameter. items.author: MatthewBonanni

items.body:
## Purpose

The HiSparse coordinator did its residency bookkeeping one page and one resident group at a time: adopting GPU copies, unpinning clean pages, planning and completing writebacks, recording copies, and freeing. Each block got its own block-pool call. A request whose whole context is GPU-resident has ~1.3k pages × 20 resident groups, so a single `schedule()` call spent tens of ms in Python, and that stalls every running request. Direct GPU landing for P/D (#55398) makes this the common case.

## Motivation

GLM shared-indexer layers reuse another layer's top-k result and do not write their own indexer keys. HiSparse currently disables the existing shared-layer index-K elision policy, so it still allocates logical-length index-K buffers for those layers. For a 78-layer GLM layout with 21 full indexers, this allocates 57 unused buffers.

## Modifications

- Add opt-in `SGLANG_ENABLE_HISPARSE_INDEX_K_ELISION=1` (default off).
- Restrict it to CUDA `glm_moe_dsa` target workers in PD decode, with PP/attention CP/DCP all 1, no external cache linker, and a valid full/shared indexer layout

Its pull waits up to `VLLM_MOONCAKE_ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT + 60` = 540 s for P's reply while holding the request's KV blocks, because ZMQ reconnects silently instead of reporting the lost peer. D also keeps the dead worker's address cached, so the requests queued behind send their pulls there and wait another 540 s. Under load, D's KV stays full of requests that can never finish.

This PR fails a pull as soon as its connection is lost, and makes D look P up again. It is the decoder-side counterpart of #64193.

items.title: [Perf] gemm: Opt-in table of pinned bit-identical cuBLASLt algorithms for BF16 linears
items.author: esarafian
items.summary: At decode batch sizes, cuBLAS's heuristic often picks a BF16 GEMM kernel whose grid leaves most SMs idle. When cuBLAS runs a GEMM without split-K, each output element is one fp32 accumulator over K, rounded once to BF16.
items.body:
## Motivation

At decode batch sizes, cuBLAS's heuristic often picks a BF16 GEMM kernel whose grid leaves most SMs idle. When cuBLAS runs a GEMM without split-K, each output element is one fp32 accumulator over K, rounded once to BF16. Other split-K-free cuBLASLt algorithms of the same library build that accumulate K in **the same order** produce the same bits while using the GPU better.

This PR lets a deployment pin such algorithms per `(N, K, M)`: an opt-in JSON table, built offline by a tuner for one GPU model and one cuBLASLt version, that unquantized BF16 linears and the BF16 `lm_head`

This creates two related interpretation problems.

## Motivation

`TokenSequenceMatcher` (`python/sglang/srt/utils/token_sequence_matcher.py`) implements a Knuth-Morris-Pratt (KMP) prefix-table automaton for online token-stream matching.

When `advance(matched, token)` is called from the terminal full-match state (`matched == len(self.pattern)`), the failure-link loop immediately indexes `self.pattern[matched]`:

```python

    matched = self.prefix_lengths[matched - 1]
```

items.title: [Perf][KV Offload] Bound copy descriptors submitted per step for CPU->GPU loads
items.author: zetxqx
items.summary: A large CPU->GPU KV offload load submits all of its copy descriptors in one call. When the call has more descriptors than the GPU command queue holds, it blocks the worker thread for most of the copy, and the next step's kernels are not launched.
items.body:
## Overview

A large CPU->GPU KV offload load submits all of its copy descriptors in one `cuMemcpyBatchAsync` call. When the call has more descriptors than the GPU command queue holds, it blocks the worker thread for most of the copy, and the next step's kernels are not launched. This PR caps the descriptors a regular async load submits per step and submits the rest in later steps.

Fixes #65515

## Claims

- Regular async loads no longer block the worker thread for the length of the copy.
- GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP=8, 8x B200, CPU tier on, AgentX c=32: 859 vs 706 output tok/s, TTFT avg 17.4 s vs 2

Prefix-LM multimodal models (Gemma 4, Gemma 3, PaliGemma, ...) attend bidirectionally inside each image or video frame. vLLM stores those blocks as one `(start, end)` span per frame in `mm_prefix_range`, and the Triton unified attention kernel loops over **every** span for every query block and every KV tile, in both `compute_tile_loop_bounds` and `compute_kv_seq_mask`. items.author: xsxszab

items.body:
## Overview

Step5 rejects `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe` with TP>1 and PP>1 at startup (`Step5 MegaMoE with TP requires sequence parallelism and PP=1`), because its model-level sequence parallelism (SP) is gated on PP=1. Step5 already handles the PP boundary under SP:
- it all-gathers its token shards before returning `IntermediateTensors` from a non-last stage;
- it re-shards them on entry to the next stage.

The default PP transport therefore sees full, TP-identical tensors, and the gate is unnecessary. This PR removes the PP=1 condition from the SP gate and the startup check.

`random-mm`'s synthetic video generator hardcodes the MP4 container encode rate at 30fps (`generate_synthetic_video`), so `--random-mm-bucket-config`'s `num_frames` does not reliably map to the frame count a target model actually processes — that depends on the model's own video preprocessing (e.g. duration-based resampling at its own native fps).

Adds `--random-mm-video-encode-fps` so the encode rate can be set to match a target model's native fps, making `num_frames` self-consistent. Backward compatible: defaults to 30.0 (the previous hardcoded value).

## Motivation

Prefill is compute-bound and sets a GPU's peak power. Long chunked-prefill passes can push a GPU into its power cap or a thermal slowdown. ## Motivation

Serving a Cosmos3 checkpoint that only fits with FSDP sharded across nodes

items.title: [Core] Handle new requests and aborts while waiting for model output
items.author: njhill
items.summary: With the multiproc executor, the engine core thread waits for each step's output by busy-polling the workers' response queues. New requests that arrive in the meantime sit in the input queue until the step completes, which with async scheduling is up to a full…
items.body:
With the multiproc executor, the engine core thread waits for each step's output by busy-polling the workers' response queues. New requests that arrive in the meantime sit in the input queue until the step completes, which with async scheduling is up to a full step later than necessary.

Instead, poll for the step's output without blocking and handle `ADD` and `ABORT` inputs from the input queue as they arrive. Any other input (e.g. a utility call) ends this early handling: it and all inputs after it are processed once the step completes, preserving their order.

## Overview

With the extensible KV cache (default on CUDA/ROCm with model runner V2, #56492), `--max-model-len auto` is fitted at planning time, against a budget that leaves out CUDA graphs and warmup on purpose: the KV cache is committed later, from the memory measured after warmup. This PR fits the length again to the measured capacity, for `auto` only.

items.author: snivertynv
items.summary: appends each decoded token with. Because is an attribute, CPython copies the whole text on every append, so each token costs O(output length) on the front-end process. [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]
items.body:
## Overview

`BaseIncrementalDetokenizer.update()` appends each decoded token with `self.output_text += piece`. Because `output_text` is an attribute, CPython copies the whole text on every append, so each token costs O(output length) on the front-end process. This PR keeps the text as buffered pieces and joins it only when read.

## Claims

- Per-step detokenizer cost no longer grows with output length for non-streaming (`FINAL_ONLY`) and streaming (`DELTA`) requests: **12.3x / 7.4x** less detokenizer time at 32k-token outputs (256 concurrent requests, CPU microbenchmark below).

# [Fix] [AMD] kimi-k3: Restore the KDA in-proj fusion for quantized checkpoints

## Motivation

On ROCm, [#35176](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35176) runs the whole KDA input projection `[q, k, v, g | f_a | b]` as one GEMM (N = 6288 per rank at TP8) for batches up to `SGLANG_ROCM_K3_FUSE_KDA_INPROJ_MAX_TOKENS` (256) tokens. Otherwise decode runs the wide `[q, k, v, g]` GEMM plus a separate `[f_a | b]` GEMV on each of Kimi-K3's 69 KDA layers. #35176 measured 0.7–2.1% more throughput and 1.0–2.6% lower median ITL from the fusion at concurrency 4–32 (ISL 8192 / OSL 1024, 8× MI355X).

items.body:
Add `dsa_cp_pack_zigzag` (`--dsa-cp-pack-zigzag`), a pack-level zigzag context-parallel layout for the DSv4 hybrid attention stack (experimental_attention_variant='dsv4_hybrid').

Under the contiguous THD split two kernels cost in proportion to the query's causal prefix: the ratio-4 indexer score + top-k (C layers) and the attend-to-all-compressed attention of the ratio-128 layers (H layers). With CP ranks the last rank does 2*CP-1 times the prefix-proportional work of the first one, and every other rank waits for it at each EP collective. With this layout rank r holds pack chunks r and 2*CP-1

## Motivation

Currently on gfx950 the two quantization options for ROCm are MXFP4 and FP8. This PR adds the middleground - MXFP6 and A6W4. They are the compromise between the two, both in speed and accuracy.


## Modifications

items.author: seansie0830
items.summary: In, when, the selected top-k values were processed in the wrong order: python [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]
items.body:
## Description
Fixes #65401.

In `LogitsProcessor.get_top_k_tokens`, when `return_log_probs=False`, the selected top-k values were processed in the wrong order:
```python
# Before (Incorrect order)
if self.scale != 1.0:
    values = values * self.scale
if self.soft_cap is not None:
    values = torch.tanh(values / self.soft_cap) * self.soft_cap
```

However, the ground truth transformation order in `forward()` applies soft capping before scaling:
```python
if logits is not None:
    if self.soft_cap is not None:
        logits = logits / self.soft_cap
        logits = torch.tanh(logits)

items.title: [Bugfix][MRv1][Spec Decode] Count NaNs in logits per request, not per logits row
items.author: DemisEom
items.summary: Fixes incorrect per-request NaN counting in vLLM V1 model runner's speculative decoding by aggregating logits rows per request instead of mapping rows directly to requests.
items.body:
## Overview

With the V1 model runner (MRV1) and speculative decoding, `VLLM_COMPUTE_NANS_IN_LOGITS` / `VLLM_RAISE_ON_LOGIT_NANS` attribute NaN counts to the wrong requests. Each request has `num_draft + 1` logits rows, but `count_nans_per_row` counts NaNs per row and `nans_to_dict` maps row `i` to request `i`, so request `j` gets row `j`'s count and rows past `num_reqs` are dropped. This PR sums each request's rows on device. It is the MRV1 counterpart of #65147 (MRV2).

Related: #63811 reported the MRV2 variant of this bug. #38506 fixed both runners together with a dict-to-ndarray refactor

items.body:
Description

MambaHybridCacheManagerV2 submits a function-local pinned staging tensor to an asynchronous host-to-device copy when preparing recurrent state indices. The local tensor has no manager-owned lifetime, so a later scheduling step can reuse the storage before the CUDA stream consumes the copy. The device can then receive state indices from a newer batch.

This change keeps the state-index staging tensor alive for the manager lifetime and fixes the race described in #21560.

items.author: nien-hui
items.summary: Fixes render endpoints dropping user-specified max_tokens from sampling_params before forwarding to the generate backend, causing the server default to be applied instead.
items.body:
## Overview

In scale-out serving, `/v1/chat/completions/render` and `/v1/completions/render` with `max_tokens` 16 return `sampling_params` without `max_tokens`, so `/inference/v1/generate` produces 700 (chat) and 40943 (completions) tokens instead of 16; a `/v1/completions/render` request without `max_tokens` defaults to 16 and takes the same path. `SamplingParams` omits fields equal to their defaults, and generate reads the absent key as not sent. `GenerateRequest` now writes `max_tokens` back into the dumped `sampling_params` when the request set it.

Fixes #65388

## Claims

- Rend

items.summary: MambaHybridCacheManagerV2 uses a temporary pinned host tensor for an asynchronous state-index copy. In setupstateindices, the persistent host state-index array is copied into a function-local staging tensor and then submitted with nonblocking=True.
items.body:
MambaHybridCacheManagerV2 uses a temporary pinned host tensor for an asynchronous state-index copy.

In _setup_state_indices(), the persistent host state-index array is copied into a function-local staging tensor and then submitted with non_blocking=True. A later scheduling step can reuse that pinned allocation before the CUDA stream has consumed the earlier copy, so the device state indices can describe a newer batch than the one being prepared.

### What does this PR do?

Allow colocated NPU rollouts to explicitly select vLLM-Ascend's native IPC loading lifecycle. Leaving the option unset preserves the existing CUDA/ROCm, shared-memory and delta dispatch paths.

DWDP local weight conversion can run out of memory while completed source shards are reclaimable. The helper currently clears the cache only after copying every shard.

items.title: Add an optional TensorAtomic placement for MCore MFSDP v2 dense parameters
items.author: Autumn1998
items.summary: Muon needs each weight matrix whole on one rank to run Newton-Schulz. MFSDP v2 shards the matrices, so today the optimizer step gathers each matrix's pieces to an owner rank and scatters the update back.
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Muon needs each weight matrix whole on one rank to run Newton-Schulz. MFSDP v2 shards the matrices, so today the optimizer step gathers each matrix's pieces to an owner rank and scatters the update back. This PR adds an optional alternative: with `MFSDP_TENSOR_ATOMIC=1`, every dense parameter stays whole on one owner rank (the `TensorAtomic` placement), so the Muon step needs no gather or scatter. Owners are chosen greedily to balance the Newton-Schulz cost. The plan depends only on parameter shapes, so every rank computes the same one. Experts keep their own mesh.

## Description

Port of #17850 (merged to `main` on 08-23) onto `feat/k3_26.08`.

The KV cache estimation pass builds temporary target and draft KV cache managers to size GPU memory. On this branch the `host_cache_size` split is skipped during estimation. So each temporary manager pins the full host tier, twice per rank with a separate draft pool, and a large host cache can run the node out of RAM at startup.

This PR estimates with `host_cache_size=0` and restores the user's value in `configure_kv_cache_capacity()`, next to the other estimation overrides (`pool_ratio`, `avg_seq_len`).

items.title: [ray] fix: prevent master port races during worker startup
items.author: SeptPonts
items.summary: Prevent during Ray worker startup caused by the gap between selecting a master port and binding PyTorch's TCPStore. Previously, probed a free port with a temporary socket, closed it, and passed the port to workers.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Prevent `EADDRINUSE` during Ray worker startup caused by the gap between selecting a master port and binding PyTorch's TCPStore.

Previously, `RayWorkerGroup` probed a free port with a temporary socket, closed it, and passed the port to workers. Another process could claim that port before rank zero initialized its process group.

Rank zero now binds and retains the actual TCPStore before invoking the user worker constructor. It publishes the bound endpoint before that constructor can block waiting for peers, allowing the driver to start the remaining ranks.

On the disaggregated server, a streamed `/v1/responses` request receives no bytes at all, not even the HTTP status line, until the context phase is done. items.body:
This PR adds --update-weight-broadcast-mode to control how full weights are broadcast to rollout engines:
- per-param (default): broadcasts each parameter separately.
- flattened-bucket: packs each update bucket into a single byte tensor and broadcasts it once, reducing collective calls.
The flattened mode preserves mixed tensor dtypes and passes load_format="flattened_bucket" to SGLang for reconstruction and loading. The configuration is also forwarded through the tensor updater’s distributed path.

Flattened broadcasting requires --update-weight-mode=full, --update-weight-transport=nccl

items.title: Fix math_dapo Minerva extraction for markdown-decorated answers
items.author: siddhant-rajhans
items.summary: The existing regex captures the markers as part of the answer, so correct answers score -1.0. Fixes #8449 ## Root cause The Minerva answer pattern matches the literal "Answer" and captures everything after the colon to end of line.
items.body:
## Bug

Models commonly wrap the Minerva `Answer:` label in markdown bold/italic (`**Answer:** 42`, `Answer: **42**`, `**Answer:**\n\n42`). The existing regex captures the `*` markers as part of the answer, so correct answers score -1.0.

Fixes #8449

## Root cause

The Minerva answer pattern `(?i)Answer\s*:\s*([^\n]+)` matches the literal "Answer" and captures everything after the colon to end of line. When models decorate with markdown:

| Input | Extracted | After normalize | Score |
|---|---|---|---|
| `**Answer:** 42` | `** 42` | `**42` | -1.0 |
| `Answer: **42**` | `**42**` | `**42**` |

items.title: Enter the paged-stash capacity reduction on every rank
items.author: Connor-XY
items.summary: When one did, a second takes the MAX of the receive capacity the step needed. Only ranks whose model chunks hold an MoE layer that reports a required capacity entered that second call: NCCL EP built in non-eager mode.
items.body:
**Why.** `PagedStashRunner.check_moe_overflow` first votes over WORLD on whether any rank went over its receive budget. When one did, a second `all_reduce` takes the MAX of the receive capacity the step needed. Only ranks whose model chunks hold an MoE layer that reports a required capacity entered that second call: NCCL EP built in non-eager mode.
- A pipeline stage made only of dense layers has no such layer, so it skipped the reduction. The MoE stages waited in it while the dense stage moved on to the rerun.
- The result is a deadlock until the NCCL timeout, or a later WORLD collective pair

**Proposal:** default `--vllm-watermark` to 0.05 for rollouts. One line in `vime/backends/vllm_utils/arguments.py`, next to the router defaults:

parser.set_defaults(vllm_watermark=0.05)

items.title: Start a chunked prefill only when its whole prompt fits
items.author: lmcafee-nvidia
items.summary: With chunked prefill enabled, the dynamic engine can stop making progress under KV-cache pressure, and never returns. lets a new request start a chunked prefill when the KV cache has room for one prompt token.
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

With chunked prefill enabled, the dynamic engine can stop making progress
under KV-cache pressure, and `generate()` never returns.
`_can_schedule_chunked_prefill()` lets a new request start a chunked
prefill when the KV cache has room for one prompt token. A long prompt can
therefore start, take the last free blocks, and then wait for one more
block. A partial chunked prefill keeps its blocks until it finishes and is
never preempted. Requests decoding beside it then pause for want of a
block. If they hold no more blocks than the paused-block budget, nothing is
evicted

items.summary: Starts all distillation teachers at once instead of one after another, which is what dominates startup when the recipe has many teachers. used to build one per teacher in a plain loop, and each constructor blocked until that teacher's vLLM servers were fully u…
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Starts all distillation teachers at once instead of one after another, which is what dominates startup when the recipe has many teachers.

`MultiTeacherModelManager` used to build one `TeacherModelManager` per teacher in a plain `for` loop, and each constructor blocked until that teacher's vLLM servers were fully up. With N teachers the wall clock was N x (engine init + CUDA graph capture). Teachers run on disjoint devices and share nothing, so this serialization was pure latency.

Measured with 8 teachers x TP=2 on 16 Ascend 910B (Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B student, vLLM roll

## Problem

For `k3` and `low_var_kl`, `compute_approx_kl` evaluates `exp(x) - 1 - x`, where `x = log_probs_base - log_probs`. This expression is nonnegative in real arithmetic, but subtracting 1 from a float32 exponential can erase the small KL term or make it negative when the policies are close.

With valid finite log-probabilities near -0.1, I reproduced a value of -1.4901161e-8 where an 80-digit reference gives 4.9986626e-11. The helper feeds the reported KL term and configured KL loss/reward paths; the Search-R1 example selects `low_var_kl` with a nonzero KL-loss coefficient.

### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8433.

`SFTTrainer` built its train/val `StatefulDataLoader`s without a `generator`, so every iterator construction drew a `base_seed` from the global CPU RNG. On resume that draw happens right after the checkpoint manager restores `torch.get_rng_state()`, so the resumed run continued from a different global CPU RNG state than an uninterrupted run. This PR gives each dataloader its own seeded `torch.Generator`, so building iterators no longer touches the global CPU RNG and the restored state is the one training actually continues with.

With `--sglang-speculative-algorithm DFLASH` and a colocated rollout engine, the first weight sync silently overwrites the DFLASH draft with target weights. After that, the acceptance length is ~1.0 and rollout is slower than with speculative decoding off.

### What does this PR do?

Adds `sharded_nixl`, a checkpoint engine for disaggregated rollout with no trainer-side all-gather. Fixes #2491

`_extract_letter_from_response` read the wrong option letter in two common reply shapes:

- `re.IGNORECASE` also applied to the `([A-Z])` letter group, so the first letter of a lowercase word counted as an answer. `The answer is definitely C.` was read as D, and `My answer is clearly D.` as C.
- It took the first match of the first pattern, and that pattern also contained `option`/`choice`. `Option A can be ruled out. The answer is C.` was read as A.

items.title: [Bug] Startup health polling can block on an unresponsive server
items.author: LinzeShi
items.summary: If the server accepts the connection but does not respond, startup polling blocks inside that request and cannot reach. This affects VIME's managed vLLM startup wait. [Discussion: independent check on main: this no longer reproduces.]
items.body:
### Bug Description

`_wait_server_healthy()` calls `requests.get(.../health)` without a timeout. If the server accepts the connection but does not respond, startup polling blocks inside that request and cannot reach `is_process_alive()`.

This affects VIME's managed vLLM startup wait. The expected behavior is to bound each probe, then check process liveness and retry while the process is alive. The overall startup wait should remain unbounded for slow model loading.

### Steps to Reproduce

items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.

## Background

Multi-model SGLang configuration was resolved incrementally while deployment side effects were already being prepared. Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.

## Problem

The config path did not validate whole-file invariants such as duplicate model names, multiple weight-updated models, complete engine topology, PP/TP consistency, or multi-node divisibility before launch.

## Solution

- Resolve every model and validate the complete config before placement or router startup.
- Reject unknown model fields

items.title: fix(sglang): bound local server startup waits
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.
items.body:
## Background

Locally managed SGLang servers are polled through `/health_generate` before rollout initialization can continue.

## Problem

The startup poll had neither a request timeout nor an overall deadline. A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.

## Solution

- Add `--sglang-server-startup-timeout` with a positive finite value and a conservative 600-second default.
- Use a monotonic deadline and cap every health request by both five seconds and the remaining startup budget.
- Reject readiness

## Background

`generate_and_rm_group` supports custom generation that fans one input out into `list[Sample]`, so a fully-async task can return `list[list[Sample]]`.

## Problem

The done callback inspected only the outer list. An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.

## Solution

- Snapshot the flat input group before generation can mutate it.
- Inspect one-level fan-out leaves for `Sample.Status.ABORTED`.
- Requeue the pristine flat snapshot

items.summary: This substantially increases peak GPU memory for long packed sequences and can cause OOMs. A Qwen3.5-4B fixed-rollout acceptance matrix completed all eight target TP/SP/CP/PP topologies, including PP=2 with four microbatches.
items.body:
## Problem

The Megatron policy and reference log-probability paths materialize
`[tokens, vocab_per_tp_rank]` logits. This substantially increases peak GPU
memory for long packed sequences and can cause OOMs.

## Changes

- Add an opt-in fused Triton backend with `--log-probs-backend triton`.
- Keep the existing PyTorch path as the default with
  `--log-probs-backend torch`.
- Support Megatron policy/reference computation with TP, SP, CP, and
  non-interleaved PP.
- Match the existing BF16 output-boundary behavior.
- Vendor the Apache-2.0 kernel from verl commit
  `4905d0cf4ebc7297231e15efa4cf

items.title: fix: restore actor weights before initial rollout sync
items.author: tengeel
items.summary: Without, initialization leaves the last auxiliary checkpoint active. Both training entry points synchronize rollout weights before the first training step, so distributed or disk-based synchronization can publish auxiliary weights instead of the resumed actor.
items.body:
## Problem

`MegatronTrainRayActor.init()` backs up the actor and then loads reference, teacher, or old-actor checkpoints into the same model.

Without `--offload-train`, initialization leaves the last auxiliary checkpoint active. Both training entry points synchronize rollout weights before the first training step, so distributed or disk-based synchronization can publish auxiliary weights instead of the resumed actor.

For one resumed run:

| | rollout logprob | reference logprob | actor logprob |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Before | -0.1106 | -0.1111 | -0.1471 |
| After | -0.1088 | -0.1421 | -0.1

items.author: LOGO127
items.summary: Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path. Under CUDA autocast, can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32.
items.body:
## Summary

Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path.

Under CUDA autocast, `torch.einsum` can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32. The result is saved for entropy backward, so the precision loss affects both the reported entropy value and its gradient.

This change keeps only that CUDA reduction outside autocast and adds a one-GPU regression suite covering FP16/BF16 autocast, masked/unmasked log-prob paths, metric-only/gradient entropy, and chunked/non-chunked execution.

Fixes #1369.

`distributed_masked_whiten(..., shift_mean=False)` used to center, scale, then add the mean back:

```

```

That is not a scale-only path. This change makes `shift_mean` do what it says:

- `shift_mean=False`: `values * rsqrt(global_var + epsilon)` — scale only; do not subtract the mean, and do not add it back

items.author: yuyz-cyber

## Problem

Training and evaluation launch rollout tasks concurrently at three levels: samples within a rollout group, rollout groups within a training batch, and samples within an evaluation batch.

When one task raises an exception, the exception is propagated but the unfinished sibling tasks are not cancelled. They can continue generation or reward computation after the rollout has failed, wasting resources and potentially leaving unobserved task exceptions in the event loop.

## Fix

At each concurrency boundary, cancel unfinished sibling tasks and wait for their cleanup before re-raising

items.title: require --ref-load when KL is enabled instead of crashing with a TypeError
items.author: rootkiller6788
items.summary: Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slimevalidateargs with, because it stat'd args.refload before checking it was set. The sibling OPD check just below already guards for None first.
items.body:
Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slime_validate_args with `TypeError: _path_exists: path should be string, bytes, os.PathLike or integer, not NoneType`, because it stat'd args.ref_load before checking it was set. The sibling OPD check just below already guards for None first.

This adds the same guard: ref_load unset now raises a ValueError telling the user to pass --ref-load, and a ref_load that points nowhere still raises the original FileNotFoundError. Two unit tests cover both cases.

items.body:
## Problem

`--rollout-temperature 0` is greedy decoding. That is not a usable on-policy RL policy: the sampling distribution is a delta, while log-probs (and PPO ratios) still come from a softmax. Greedy RL should be rejected at config parse, not assumed away in loss code.

`--eval-temperature 0` is unchanged; greedy eval remains valid.

## Change

`slime_validate_args` raises if `rollout_temperature <= 0`.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/test_megatron_argument_validation.py` — `0.0` and `-0.1` raise; existing validate-args cases still pass at the default `1.0`

instead of:

`http://[2001:db8::1]:8000/health`

The health check may then keep retrying failed requests, making engine

items.author: Henry-Jessie
items.summary: This PR reduces actor-update memory usage when entropy is logged but does not contribute to the loss. Long-context actor updates can become memory-bound because entropy is evaluated over the full vocabulary.
items.body:
## Summary

This PR reduces actor-update memory usage when entropy is logged but does not contribute to the loss.

Long-context actor updates can become memory-bound because entropy is evaluated over the full vocabulary. When `entropy_coef == 0`, VIME still computes entropy metrics, but the entropy tensor is only used for reporting and has no gradient contribution. The current implementation always builds the entropy autograd graph and clones the full logits tensor before entropy computation, which increases peak memory without changing the loss.

## Summary

This PR fixes a hang in non-colocated full NCCL weight sync when the Megatron actor uses pipeline parallelism, for example `--tensor-model-parallel-size 1 --pipeline-model-parallel-size 2`.

The root cause is that Vime treated every `DP=0, TP=0` pipeline stage as a vLLM weight-sync source rank. With `PP>1`, multiple trainer ranks concurrently initialized separate trainer-to-vLLM NCCL transfer groups against the same vLLM rollout engines.
